content: {"summary":"ENOSPC errors on kafka-02 when writing to /var indicate the root filesystem is out of space, even though the Kafka data directory (/data/kafka) appears healthy.","likely_cause":"/var partition is full, most likely due to accumulated Kafka GC logs or other large logs on the root disk.","confidence":"high","claims":[{"text":"ENOSPC on a broker can stem from either the data volume or the root disk, so the first step is to identify which is full.","evidence_ids":["INC-0070#3"],"quote":"the first job is to find out which is full."},{"text":"In a similar case the root disk was full because GC logs were written there.","evidence_ids":["INC-0070#3"],"quote":"here it was the root disk, because the GC logs live there."},{"text":"Kafka GC logs are stored under /var/log/kafka and can consume the /var filesystem if not rotated.","evidence_ids":["RB-008#2"],"quote":"Broker GC logs live in `/var/log/kafka`. Rotate them; don't touch `/data/kafka`"},{"text":"The system journal can occupy significant space on /var and can be reduced with journalctl commands.","evidence_ids":["RB-008#1"],"quote":"journalctl --disk-usage, then sudo journalctl --vacuum-size=500M"},{"text":"Deleted files that remain open keep space allocated; lsof +L1 can reveal such processes.","evidence_ids":["RB-008#1"],"quote":"A process still has it open: `sudo lsof +L1`"}],"next_checks":["Run `df -h /var` to confirm which filesystem is full.","Check journal size with `journalctl --disk-usage` and clean with `journalctl --vacuum-size=500M`.","List large files in /var/log (e.g., `du -sh /var/log/*`) focusing on Kafka GC logs in /var/log/kafka.","Rotate or truncate Kafka GC logs; ensure logrotate is configured for /var/log/kafka.","Run `sudo lsof +L1` to find processes holding deleted files and restart or truncate them.","Verify that /data/kafka remains under capacity after addressing /var issues."]}
